source.title_on_document: Has AI Surpassed Humans in Creative Idea Generation? A Meta-Analysis

supplement.holds: The full systematic search strategy, the extracted data (effect sizes and sample variances), and the meta-analysis scripts; per-study effect sizes are not tabulated in the main text

paper_design_summary: A three-level meta-analysis of 15 articles (17 studies, 115 effect sizes) made available January 2022 to January 2025 that compare ideas generated by humans with ideas generated by prompting GenAI with similar instructions and no further interaction. Effect sizes are Cohen's d on blind assessments of overall creativity, originality, or usefulness, coded so that positive values favor GenAI. Studies of people working with AI (co-creation) are excluded, and no diversity or homogenization outcome is analyzed.

studies.label: Three-level meta-analysis of human vs. GenAI-prompted idea generation (15 articles, 17 studies, 115 effect sizes)

participants.who: Corpus of 15 articles contributing 17 studies and 115 effect sizes (January 2022 to January 2025). Human comparison groups in the primary studies were students, crowdworkers, or experts (Table 1, p. 7); the meta-analysis reports no pooled participant count.
participants.quote: Finally, 15 articles contributing 17 studies and 115 effect sizes could be included in the meta-analysis.

ai_tool.name_model: 14 distinct (large) language models plus one diffusion model (DALL·E 2), including GPT-3, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Claude 3.5, Bard, Perplexity, Copy.ai, Jurassic-1 (p. 10, Section 4.2; Table 1, p. 7)
ai_tool.how_used: GenAI was prompted alone with instructions similar to those given to humans, with no further interaction; comparisons with people using GenAI dialogically (co-creation) were excluded (p. 6, Section 3.2).

task.description: Creative idea generation tasks in the primary studies: alternate uses task, business ideas for the circular economy, app and product invention ideas, sustainable product ideas, children's toy ideas, alien-character sketch ideas, everyday-problem solutions, NLP research ideas, survival, bicycle, and app ideas (Table 1, p. 7).

outcomes.name: Pooled creativity difference, all indices (overall creativity, originality, usefulness; blind assessments), GenAI vs. humans
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Mixed measurement pool: human evaluations, including expert ratings, and automated originality scores. The human_raters code identifies only the human-rating component, not the entire pool. The supplementary dataset includes 'Originality (human evaluation)' (Sheet1, rows 21-25), 'Originality (AI evaluation)' (rows 26-30), 'Semantic distance' (rows 31-33 and 115), and 'Creativity (expert ratings)' (row 36). Semantic distance between an idea and its corresponding object is an automated originality score, not a measure of similarity across different people (PsyArXiv v2, p. 4, Section 2.3; p. 7, Table 1). Supplement: dataset.xlsx, https://osf.io/download/3yvpz/, read in memory.

contrasts.reported: Three-level meta-analysis, 115 effect sizes: d = .360, 95% CI [-.071, .790]; Q(df = 114) = 2516.39, p < .001. Without 14 influential values: d = .236, 95% CI [-.073, .544]; Q(df = 100) = 1661.00, p < .001. Positive d favors GenAI.

outcomes.name: Usefulness indices (reference category of the construct moderator), GenAI vs. humans
outcomes.question: none

contrasts.reported: Usefulness: 32 effect sizes from 10 studies. Table 2 intercept (usefulness = reference): complete dataset d = .175, 95% CI [-.286, .635]; without influential values d = .147, 95% CI [-.189, .482].

outcomes.name: Originality indices, difference relative to usefulness (construct moderator), GenAI vs. humans
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Mixed originality measures: human evaluations and automated_score measures, including AI evaluations and semantic-distance originality scores. The human_raters code identifies only the human-rating component. The supplementary dataset includes 'Originality (human evaluation)' (Sheet1, rows 21-25), 'Originality (AI evaluation)' (rows 26-30), and 'Semantic distance' (rows 31-33 and 115), all coded as originality in the creativity_component column. The paper describes semantic distance between each idea and its corresponding object as a proxy for originality (PsyArXiv v2, p. 4, Section 2.3; p. 7, Table 1). Supplement: dataset.xlsx, https://osf.io/download/3yvpz/, read in memory.

contrasts.reported: Originality: 42 effect sizes from 14 studies. Relative to usefulness: complete dataset d = .323, 95% CI [.040, .606]; without influential values d = .173, 95% CI [-.081, .352]. Test of moderation Qm(df = 2) = 5.03, p = .081 (complete); Qm(df = 2) = 1.78, p = .410 (without influential values).

outcomes.name: Creativity as a single construct, difference relative to usefulness (construct moderator), GenAI vs. humans
outcomes.question: none

contrasts.reported: Creativity as a singular construct: 41 effect sizes from 7 studies. Relative to usefulness: complete dataset d = .144, 95% CI [-.161, .448]; without influential values d = .088, 95% CI [-.176, .352].

outcomes.name: Pooled creativity difference, ChatGPT models only (GPT-4, GPT-3.5, GPT-3), vs. humans
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Mixed measurement pool: human evaluations, including expert ratings, and automated semantic-distance originality scores. The human_raters code identifies only the human-rating component. The supplementary dataset includes 'Semantic distance' for GPT-4 (Sheet1, rows 31-32) and GPT-3 (row 115), and 'Creativity (expert ratings)' for GPT-3.5 (row 36); these models enter the ChatGPT subset (PsyArXiv v2, p. 10, Section 4.2). Semantic-distance scoring compares an idea with its corresponding object (p. 4, Section 2.3). Supplement: dataset.xlsx, https://osf.io/download/3yvpz/, read in memory.

contrasts.treatment_arm: Ideas generated by prompting ChatGPT (GPT-4, GPT-3.5, GPT-3)
contrasts.reported: 65 effect sizes from 13 studies: d = .478, 95% CI [-.040, .996]; Q(df = 64) = 1825.73, p < .001. Without 2 influential values: d = .374, 95% CI [-.047, .975]. Version moderator (Table 3, GPT-4 = reference): intercept .554 [-.019, 1.128]; GPT-3.5 -.220 [-.726, .286]; GPT-3 -.476 [-2.506, 1.554]; Qm(df = 2) = .90, p = .637 (without influential values Qm(df = 2) = .92, p = .631).

synthesis.search_end: January 2025 (search window January 2022 to January 2025; p. 5, Section 3.1)
synthesis.inclusion: Studies that experimentally compared ideas generated by humans with ideas generated by prompting GenAI with similar instructions and no further interaction (co-creation excluded), on discrete idea generation, with overall creativity, originality, or usefulness assessed by evaluators blind to the ideas' origin, in English, with statistics allowing a meta-analysis (p. 6, Section 3.2). 15 articles, 17 studies.

eligibility.reason: This is a meta-analysis with no original randomized study assigning people to AI assistance. Its included comparisons require separate human and prompted-GenAI idea generation without further interaction and exclude computational co-creativity (PsyArXiv v2, p. 5, Section 3; p. 6, Section 3.2), so criterion 1 is not met. No pooled count of people analyzed is reported; the reported counts are studies and effect sizes, so criterion 2 cannot be established from them (p. 7, Section 3.4; pp. 9-10, Sections 4.1-4.2). The underlying outcomes assess creativity, originality, or usefulness of generated ideas using human evaluations and automated scores, satisfying the output-scoring criterion (p. 6, Section 3.2; p. 4, Section 2.3; supplementary dataset.xlsx, Sheet1, rows 21-36 and 114-116). The paper remains synthesis context and analyzes no diversity or homogenization outcome.

one_line_finding: Across 17 studies (115 effect sizes) comparing ideas from prompted GenAI with human ideas, the pooled difference favoring GenAI was small and not significant, d = .360, 95% CI [-.071, .790] (d = .236 without 14 influential values), and for ChatGPT alone d = .478, 95% CI [-.040, .996] (PsyArXiv v2, pp. 8 and 10).
notes: The meta-analysis analyzes effect-size estimates. None of the available output-unit categories applies, and the number of condition-level output sets is not reported, so unit and n_units are null for all outcomes. The effect-size counts remain explicitly labeled in contrasts.reported and synthesis (PsyArXiv v2, p. 7, Section 3.4; p. 8, Section 3.5; pp. 9-10, Sections 4.1-4.2). For the mixed measurement pools, human_raters identifies one component; measure_detail records the additional automated and, where documented, expert assessments.
